findings.description: Activation can select an invalid task plan that lacks a design.
findings.analysis: The workflow says activation selects the deepest valid planning artifact and that tasks require a design, but it currently selects build whenever tasks.md exists. A malformed or legacy queued task plan could therefore bypass the design guard.
findings.recommendation: Vary. Activation deterministically fills the preparation chain before build.
findings.rationale: Activation must ensure estimate, design, and tasks exist in that order, invoking the first missing preparation step. It may invoke build only when all three planning artifacts exist; a task plan without design is therefore reconciled after design rather than treated as build-ready.
